correctness.rationale: The proof uses the unique Gaussian top-r set T (uniform over N), and conditional on forbidden T the unique cheapest one-coordinate swap to T′. Johnson independence ensures T′ is permitted. Its missing min-in/max-out elements are independently uniform among r and s options, giving per-permitted-basis selection probability N^{-1}(1+d(B)/(rs)). Squaring and using sum d=lambda rs plus sum d^2=lambda rs+8mu (four common Johnson neighbors for any distance-two forbidden pair) yields the stated collision formula. Rook-grid independent-set bound d<=min(r,s) gives the sharp global range. Independently enumerated all 720 Gaussian coordinate orderings for n=6,r=3 for two nonbasis pairs, reproducing 18 times 1/18 and spectrum (4 at 1/20, 10 at 1/18, 4 at 11/180), with collision values 1/18 and 113/2025. Finite checks are not a general proof; the all-n argument is the counting proof.
